references.text: Parallel law text in Deuteronomy that repeats the prohibition against eating camel because it chews the cud but does not have split hooves, and is therefore unclean.
Previous verse establishing the criteria for clean animals: they must both have completely split hooves and chew the cud.
Continuation of the list of unclean animals that meet only one of the two criteria for cleanliness, including the rock badger, hare, and pig.
First mention of camels in the Bible, showing that the Israelites knew these animals from the time of the patriarchs.
Prophetic warning against those who eat unclean things, indicating that dietary laws had lasting significance.
